title: Replay and external data: separate pools, limits on age and distance, and a floor on the effective sample size
design_ref: Replay buffers and data from other policies
purpose: Mix the policy's own older data and human-written solutions into the batches at set shares, with the design's limits, and watch what each does to the effective sample size, the entropy and the held-out score. Then let the effective-sample-size floor lower the replay share by itself.

steps.display: python pool_report.py pools-s07   # per run: the share of micro-batches from each pool and what each pool's data looked like to the trainer

checks.because: Six recipes through the research queue.

checks.description: each pool's share of the micro-batches is close to its setting (replay 15% and 40%, external 5% and 40%, to within seven points)
checks.because: Each micro-batch comes from one pool, chosen by a credit counter so that the shares are met exactly, not on average: 15% means every seventh batch. A pool that has nothing eligible passes its turn to fresh data, so replay can fall short at the start while the pool fills.

checks.description: replay obeys its limits: no replayed batch is older than the age limit or further from the policy than the KL limit
checks.because: A stored batch is eligible only while its age is within 40 versions and its behavior KL to the current policy, computed with the current weights when it is picked, is at most 0.05. The rest are retired; the table shows how many.

checks.description: replayed data is further off-policy than fresh data: its effective sample size is lower
checks.because: A replayed batch is older, so its samples come from policies further from the current one, and its importance weights are more uneven.

checks.description: external solutions go through their own small loss: the policy's loss on them falls during training
checks.because: Human-written tokens are very unlikely under the policy, so their importance weights would explode in the RL loss. They get a plain negative-log-likelihood term at a small weight instead, and the policy gradually absorbs them.

checks.description: the effective-sample-size floor lowered the replay share by itself at least once, and recorded why
checks.because: The rule watches the micro-batch ESS. When it stays under the floor for three steps it halves the replay share and gives the difference back to fresh data; each action is an event with the metric values that triggered it. After thirty healthy steps the share climbs back one notch at a time, never above the recipe's setting.

notes: Entropy over the last 20 steps: fresh 0.264, replay15 0.385, replay40 0.427, external5 0.396, external40 0.603, replay40-floor 0.345. Held-out pass rate at the end: fresh 0.583, replay15 0.547, replay40 0.511, external5 0.541, external40 0.381, replay40-floor 0.526.
